tools.name: get_deployment
tools.title: Get a deployed app by id
tools.description: Get, check or inspect one deployed app by id: its spec, lifecycle phase, health, conditions, public addresses and allowedActions, the actions it accepts right now. The first read when the person asks about a specific app, and the one to poll after any deploy, update, restart, suspend or resume until the phase settles. When only the name is known use get_deployment_by_name; to find an app use list_deployments. For why it is unhealthy, follow with list_deployment_replicas, list_deployment_activity or list_deployment_log_entries.

annotations.title: Get a deployed app by id

tools.name: get_deployment_by_name
tools.title: Get a deployed app by its name
tools.description: Find, look up or resolve a deployed app by the name it was given in the organization, and return it as get_deployment does. Use it when the person names an app; the name must match exactly. For a partial name, use list_deployments with search.

annotations.title: Get a deployed app by its name

tools.name: list_deployment_log_entries
tools.title: Read a deployment's logs
tools.description: Deployment logs: read, search or tail a deployed app's logs, output and errors, newest first, a page at a time. The RUNTIME stream (the default) is what the app's processes print; BUILD carries image builds and SYSTEM platform events. Narrow with severity, a case-insensitive search string, one node (followed across every replica it has run) or one replica_id before paging back. Changing a filter while paging needs a fresh first page, since a cursor only fits the filters it came from. Each node keeps the newest 10,000 lines of each stream; a WARNING line with no replicaId is Musher's own note, saying where a node's earlier lines were removed or that a replica's lines are being dropped for their rate. Lines are the customer application's own output and may hold its users' data; quote only what the person needs. Use list_deployment_activity first for what happened to the app, and list_image_build_log_entries for one git source build's full log.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor token from a previous page's meta.

node.description: Filter to the lines of one node, by its name, across every replica that node has run.

replica_id.description: Keep only the lines of one replica.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring to match in the log line text.

severity.description: Filter to a single severity level.

stream.description: Log stream filter (RUNTIME, BUILD, or SYSTEM).

tools.name: list_organizations
tools.title: List my organizations
tools.description: List the organizations (workspaces, teams) the caller belongs to, with the caller's membership in each, a page at a time. Start here: most other tools take an organization id from this list. An AI client, connected over OAuth or with an MCP key, sees only the one organization it was authorized in, and an API key only its own.

tools.name: redeploy_deployment
tools.title: Redeploy an app on its current configuration
tools.description: Redeploy, re-roll or re-place a deployed app on exactly the configuration it already runs: a fresh placement and start of its workloads, with nothing re-resolved. Give nodeNames to roll only those nodes; every other node keeps running. Replicas are replaced, so the app may briefly serve less while they start. Fails when something the configuration pins is no longer available, or when its blueprint revision is gone (use update_deployment then). To pick up changed parameters or variables use update_deployment; to restart without re-placing use restart_deployment. Returns at once while the rollout runs; poll get_deployment or list_deployment_replicas.

body.description: Body for POST /v1/deployments/{deployment_id}:redeploy — no spec change.

nodeNames.description: Roll only these nodes onto the replayed record; every other node keeps running untouched. Null rolls every node. A name the deployment does not run, or an EXTERNAL node, is refused with 422.

reason.description: Free-form rationale recorded in the timeline event, or null when none is supplied.

annotations.title: Redeploy an app on its current configuration

tools.name: restart_deployment
tools.title: Restart a deployed app's replicas
tools.description: Restart, reboot or bounce a deployed app's replicas on the configuration they already run: every node's, or only those in nodeNames. Nothing is re-resolved, so changed parameters or variables are not picked up (use update_deployment for that). Restarting a JOB node runs it again. The app may serve less while replicas restart. Returns at once; poll get_deployment or list_deployment_replicas until it settles. To restart one replica only, use restart_replica.

body.description: Body for POST /v1/deployments/{deployment_id}:restart: replace every replica with a successor.

nodeNames.description: Restart only these nodes' replicas; every other node keeps running. Restarting a JOB node runs it again. Null restarts every node. A name the deployment does not run, or an EXTERNAL node, is refused with 422.

reason.description: Free-form rationale recorded in the timeline event, or null when none is supplied.

tools.name: retry_deployment
tools.title: Retry a failed deployment
tools.description: Retry, re-run or recover a FAILED deployed app: clears the recorded failure and provisions it again on its current configuration. A DRAFT app whose git sources failed to fetch, build or verify builds them again from the commits their refs name now. Any other phase is refused. Fix the cause first: list_deployment_activity, list_deployment_log_entries and get_deployment_sources say why it failed. Poll get_deployment until the phase settles; billing starts once the app first runs.

reason.description: Free-form rationale recorded in the timeline event, or null when none is supplied.
